YOUR COMPANION, NOT YOUR INSTRUCTIONS

Help for your next experiment.

  1. Build the circuit you’re reading about. Choose Add component, then click or tap the canvas to place it. Drag a part by its body or name to move it. Click two gold pins, or drag from one pin to another, to make a wire. The Pins tab offers larger targets; the Details tab holds component properties. The canvas keeps going in every direction. Drag empty space to pan; Fit brings your whole circuit back into view. Connected pins have labels. Select a wire to highlight both ends; use Pin labels to hide the extra labels.
  2. Write the JavaScript yourself. The editor starts empty. The Uno runs real Johnny-Five over Firmata. Add JavaScript files when the book uses local modules such as Rover.js.
  3. Run, observe, and experiment. Run starts a fresh board. The console accepts commands for objects added using this.repl.inject(...). Stop also works if your code gets stuck.
  4. Save your work. Download and Open use project files. Share creates a link containing your code and circuit. Shared projects never run automatically.
Use the book’s code, with fewer setup steps.

The lab provides the supported libraries and starts the virtual board when you press Run. You can skip Arduino serial-port setup and Firmata uploading here. Choose the board used in the chapter, and check its coverage below.

What’s simulated?

Wiring, pin signals, introductory resistor networks, sensors and peripheral behavior. This is a learning model; it does not model component damage, mains electricity, or every physical effect.

Use the book’s diagrams and code to make your own project. This guide shows which exercises the lab can run and where an adaptation is needed. Chapter text and illustrations stay in the book. Program checks cover code and observable output; circuit review and physical setup are separate.

Program checkedPartial coverageMore work needed

Requirements checked against Lyza Gardner’s official example source. Examples keep their original attribution. Coverage is measured per example, not promised for an entire chapter.

Optional starting points. You can load only the code and wire it yourself, or explore a prepared circuit. Loading an example can be undone.

Your own little lab.

A construction workspace for learning JavaScript and electronics. Add parts, write code, and follow your own ideas—or work alongside JavaScript on Things.

The Uno uses real Johnny-Five, Firmata firmware and AVR8js processor emulation. Component visuals come from Wokwi and original models. Open Help to check chapter and example coverage.

The lab is independent and is not affiliated with Manning, Arduino, Wokwi, or Velxio. The book’s later chapters use other boards and services; their status is shown explicitly in Help.

Code runs on this device in a worker. Stop terminates it. This is not a general Node.js terminal or an electrical safety tool.
